'''''Cordyline petiolaris''''', known as the '''broad leaved palm lily''' is an [[evergreen]] [[Australia]]n plant. A shrub to around 5 metres tall. Found in warm [[rainforest]] and moist [[eucalyptus]] forest.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://asgap.org.au/c-pet.html |title=Cordyline petiolaris |accessdate=2010-05-17 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070901210039/http://asgap.org.au/c-pet.html |archivedate=2007-09-01 }}</ref> The range of natural distribution is from the [[Nambucca River]] to near [[Gladstone, Queensland]].

Leaves 30 to 80 cm long, and 4 to 12 cm wide,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?page=nswfl&lvl=sp&name=Cordyline~petiolaris|title = PlantNET - FloraOnline}}</ref> elliptic in shape. Leaves on long unrolled leaf stalks. The species name ''petiolaris'' refers to these long stems.

Flowering occurs from late winter to spring, being white or lilac in colour. Fruit is a red berry, 7 to 10 mm in diameter. The fruit can persist on the plant for many months. This species propagates easily from seeds or stem cuttings.

Not as widely seen in cultivation as ''[[Cordyline australis]]'', however it is also well suited to gardens with moist soils in semi shade. It is not frost tolerant. Also suited as an indoor [[pot plant]].
